title: Capacity heartbeat & priming rituals - weekly checkin
summary: Weekly capture of capacity heartbeat metrics, planned priming windows, 'priming ritual' experiments, and action items. Focus this week: reduce cold-start latency for small-chat workloads in eu-west while preserving spare capacity for bursty hosted traffic.
metrics_snapshot: current_reserved_burst_pool: 38 GPUs (used for scheduled bursts and canaries)
notes:
Background and framing:
- We continue to see recurring tail-latency spikes in eu-west1 for short-chat (<150 token) requests during region-specific marketing pushes. Root cause appears multifactorial: cold KV cache, small-batch packing inefficiency, and a recent scheduler tweak that reduced spur capacity for low-priority routes.

This doc captures the cadence and 'rituals' we're trialing for priming/heartbeat prep and the weekly health snapshot. Goal: lower p90 for short-chat to <100ms without increasing global spend by >3%.

Key observations this week:
- eu-west1 p90 at 120ms (+15% week-over-week). Heatmap shows spikes aligning with marketing campaign start times (08:00-11:00 UTC).
- KV cache hit-rate for short-chat models in eu-west1: 62% (target 80% for warm-state).
- Autoscaler smoothing window changed last week by release ENGOPS-493; that lowered spur capacity assignments for 'low-priority' routes. We reverted part of change but need formal rollback test.
- Priming bursts deployed as a cron prewarm (2x 2-minute bursts at 07:45 and 08:15 UTC) reduced initial 90th by ~18% in small A/B canary but consumed an extra average of 3.2 GPU-hours/day in the region.

Decisions made in session:
- Trial a staggered compact priming ritual for eu-west1 for the next 7 days: three short bursts (07:30, 07:50, 08:10 UTC) using prioritized prefix cache keys rather than full inference workloads to keep token usage low.
- Cap nightly priming to 4 GPU-hours/region and route; if experiment exceeds 4h/day we'll throttle. Objective is to keep cost delta <2.5%.
- Re-run autoscaler smoothing rollback test on staging with controlled traffic shape (INFRA-1310) before wider rollback.
- Schedule a focused postmortem if p90 doesn't improve below 110ms after 7-day trial.

Experiment plan (Priming ritual details):
- Burst content: 60-90s sequences of synthetic short-chat prompts designed to warm KV cache for top-10 prefixes. Use low-token payloads and a dedicated priming API key tagged 'priming/eu-west1'.
- Traffic shaping: bursts run from our seeding hosts in eu-west1 to avoid cross-region noise.
- Monitoring: add a temporary dashboard panel for priming-induced cost (gpu-hours by priming-key), and a tagged trace to identify priming vs real-traffic.
- Canary targets: run priming on 10% of capacity first (4 GPUs) for 48 hours, evaluate hit-rates and p90, then ramp to 25% if stable.

Incidents and recent mitigations:
- Incident: 2026-06-07 08:05 UTC — transient spike in eu-west1 due to high influx from campaign + autoscaler smoothing change. Mitigation: manual trigger of spare-pool assignment and short-term override (Connor). Follow-up: add guardrail to never drop spare below 6% for regions with active marketing tags. (Action item below).

Blockers / Risks:
- If priming consumes more spare pool than expected during a global surge, it could reduce capacity for high-priority customers. Need reserve gating.
- KV warmup tooling currently lacks fine-grained prefix targeting; engineering effort required (estimate 3 dev-days) to implement prefix seeding.
- Observability gaps: cost attribution of priming vs real traffic needs clearer tagging in tracing pipeline.

Action items (owners + due dates):
